result.title: Expected result
result.empty: Choose a state, a district and a scheme to see a result.
result.rangeNote: Plan with the range, not the middle value.
result.fromModel: Model assumption: change from the real settings, {{central}} pp (range {{weak}} to {{strong}} pp)
result.noReasons: No setting differs from the real scheme.
result.error: Could not get a result. Try again.
result.invalid: These settings are not allowed for this scheme.

warning.survey_estimate: Based on a household survey (NFHS), not official sign-up counts. District values carry sampling error and cover more than this scheme alone.
warning.low_confidence: The range is wider than 30 percentage points. Treat this result with caution.
warning.new_policy: This is a new policy, far from any real scheme. The range is wider.
warning.out_of_range: Beyond what real schemes do: a setting is outside the values of real schemes, so the model is less certain.
warning.partial_data: This result uses state-level figures (bank accounts, income) that are the same for every district in the state.

compare.title: Compare two settings
compare.intro: Same district, two settings. The difference is B minus A.
compare.empty: Choose a state and a district to compare two settings.
compare.diffNote: Both settings share the same NFHS value and sampling error, so only the model's effect of the sliders differs. The range covers the weak, central and strong model sets.
compare.diffOtherScheme: No difference is shown: A and B are different schemes, which measure different things.
compare.diffOtherBase: No difference is shown: a custom policy is measured within its target group, a real scheme across everyone. They cannot be compared.

report.title: Model report
report.intro: How accurate the model is, what it assumes, and where it is weak. Every number comes from the latest training run.
report.beats: The agent model beats the baseline.
report.notBeats: The agent model does not beat the simple baseline (GBM).
report.role: So district levels come from NFHS data. The agent model is used only for how much a slider change moves the result.
report.noDataDistricts: Districts without a result (of all listed)
report.accIntro: Mean absolute error in percentage points on held-out NFHS-5 values. Lower is better.
report.wins: The agent model is better than the baseline in {{wins}} of {{folds}} states.
report.losoNote: Only {{schemes}} schemes, so this test is weak: a held-out scheme has slider values never seen in training.
report.betaIntro: b2 benefit value relative to income, b3 documents (illiterate), b5 application burden, b6 speed, b8 bank account (fixed, assumed by team); b0 baseline, b7 district deprivation, era_shift NFHS-4 to NFHS-5 (fitted).
report.recTitle: Can the fitting find known values?
report.recIntro: Data was simulated with known values, then the fit was run again. The error should be small.
report.bandNote: The range on the Simulator adds this survey error to the spread of the three model sets.
report.sanityIntro: Median district, starting from its real NFHS-5 value. Each cell: weak / central / strong.
report.method: A slider change moves the district's real NFHS-5 level up or down on a log-odds scale, by the average effect of that change on the people the scheme is for.

weak.agentNotBetter: The agent model is less accurate than the baseline for district levels ({{agent}} vs {{gbm}} pp error), and better in only {{wins}} of {{folds}} states.
weak.loso: The leave-one-scheme-out test has only {{schemes}} schemes, so it says little.
weak.fixedBetas: The weights for benefit value, documents, bank account, burden and speed are assumed by the team, not estimated from data. The range covers three sets (weak, central, strong).
weak.deff: The survey design effect is {{deff}}, {{label}}. The NFHS sheets do not print it.
weak.jsyBirths: The JSY survey band uses estimated births (women interviewed times a 2011 Census ratio), not a printed count. Half-width: median ±{{median}} pp, largest ±{{max}} pp.
weak.jsyBirthsNoNumbers: The JSY survey band uses estimated births, not a printed count.
weak.nfhsDrop: In {{n}} of {{of}} districts, PM-JAY coverage in NFHS-5 is at or below NFHS-4 ({{nOwn}} of {{ofOwn}} districts that have their own NFHS-4 value; the rest use the state value), and in some it is much lower (for example in Arunachal Pradesh). We do not know whether coverage really fell or the two surveys measured it differently.
weak.partial: {{n}} training rows use a state-level baseline instead of a district value.
weak.noData: {{n}} of {{total}} listed districts have no result; {{unmapped}} of them are new districts with no 2011 parent.
weak.noDataLoading: The count of districts without a result is loading.
weak.survey: Results are survey estimates (NFHS), not official sign-up counts.
weak.boundaries: District boundaries are approximate and not authoritative.

about.title: About and data
about.disclaimer: A planning aid, not a guarantee.
about.what: GovSim lets officials test a welfare scheme before launch. Pick a district and a scheme, move the sliders, and see the expected uptake as a range. The district level comes from survey data; the model only estimates how much a change moves it.

nfhs.name: NFHS-5 and NFHS-4 district fact sheets
nfhs.credit: International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS) and Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. Obtained from The DHS Program (dhsprogram.com).

limit.survey: Values are survey estimates with sampling error, not official sign-up counts.
limit.range: Always plan with the range, not the middle value.
limit.proxy: Each scheme is measured by a survey proxy (for example, clean cooking fuel for PMUY), which covers more than the scheme alone.
limit.census: Population bases are from the 2011 Census and are more than ten years old.
limit.boundaries: District boundaries are approximate and not authoritative.
limit.model: Effects of the sliders are model assumptions with weakly estimated weights, not measured results.
